Name: Colonist And Bots Auto Upgrade
Description:
[h3]NOT COMPATIBLE WITH V0.14![/h3]

CARAU finds compatible replacement body parts in available inventory and queues ordinary Stardeus surgery or assembly work. Review one Being, queue a specific operation, or plan an ordered batch.

[h2]How to Open CARAU[/h2]
- The permanent CARAU top-bar icon opens or closes the main interface.
- The Tracked Operations widget appears only while CARAU has active operations, retry waits, or retained failures.
- An optional keyboard shortcut can be assigned in Settings.

[h2]Current Features[/h2]
[h3]Upgrade Assistance[/h3]
- Independently enables or disables higher-Tier and same-tier Quality upgrades while preserving tier-first selection
- Uses available compatible inventory and re-evaluates each slot after queueing
- Supports living biological and mechanical Beings, plus non-missing-part maintenance of dead mechanical Beings
- Does not automate operations on dead biological Beings
- Excludes hostile housed minds from automatic Core and Brain selection
- Avoids Destroyed slots, non-removable parts, unsafe parent chains, and reserved inventory
- Prevents automated work while a selected Being is temporarily untargetable during a Mental Breakdown

[h3]Preventative Implants[/h3]
- Optional, default-off Mood Regulator surgery follows Mental Breakdown interruptions
- Optional, default-off Firewall Chip surgery responds when a living player-owned mechanical Being is being hacked
- Both require an empty usable Implant slot, available inventory, and the automatic surgery threshold; CARAU never replaces an installed Implant
- CARAU-created preventative procedures appear in Tracked Operations

[h3]Configurable Automatic Retry[/h3]
- Manual, Transient, and Transient + Surgery policies control recognized automatic retries
- Manual is the safe default; manual queue and retry actions remain outside automatic limits
- Shared automatic-attempt limit ranges from 0 to 10 and defaults to 3
- Automatic surgery retry requires a fresh operator-neutral Stardeus estimate strictly above the configured 0-100% threshold, default 90%
- Every retry rechecks slot policy, Quality, inventory, reservations, ownership, removability, body state, welded state, and native queueability
- Progressive retry waits never execute while paused and remain visible in Tracked Operations
- Death, destroyed slots, welded installed parts, stale ownership, external cancellation, invalid targets, and unknown failures are never retried automatically
- Automatic retry never attempts post-death Core recovery; destructive welded-part removal is manual and confirmation-only

[h3]Welded-Part Recovery[/h3]
- Shows every installed welded slot with Quality, Condition, and state
- On an idle, player-owned mechanical Being, a confirmed manual action can destroy any welded unusable part and its slot
- A welded usable Core is also eligible when every Battery or every Mobilizer slot is welded/unusable; multi-slot groups require every slot
- Uses native extraction cleanup, preserves the Core mind, and never enters batch or retry automation

[h3]Main Tab and Batch Processing[/h3]
- Select, review, and reorder multiple Beings in a responsive scrollable list
- Reordering controls exact order-aware batch planning and execution
- Batch Queue displays a validated live operation count across all selected Beings
- Switch between selected Beings without losing scroll position
- Responsive body-part cards show icons, names, Quality, Condition, states, actions, and detailed tooltips
- Queue one operation, every operation for one Being, or the complete planned batch
- Limits Install Missing actions to living Beings
- Offers selected-Being and Queue All Remove All Parts actions when every present Battery, Core, or Mobilizer slot in a group is destroyed or contains an unusable welded part
- Uses Stardeus's native Remove All Parts procedure; destroyed, welded, and otherwise non-removable parts remain in place
- Pending procedures remain visible with reserved replacement details

[h3]Tracked Operations[/h3]
- Tracks only surgical and assembly operations scheduled by CARAU
- Persistent records survive save and load without leaking across games
- Dedicated resizable window follows the exact planned Being order
- Scrollable Being list preserves its position during selection and operation removal
- Live cards show targeted slots, replacements, retry waits, failures, preventative implants, and native Remove All Parts mass operations
- Validates the projected installed result before accepting a native outcome
- Captures native surgical failures, including operatorless automated surgeries
- Targets Core's current surgical-failure overload explicitly so rc313 tracking initialization remains unambiguous
- Handles Core identity transitions without treating a successful mind swap as body death
- Retains failed Being and slot cards until acknowledged
- Cancels remaining CARAU operations if a tracked Being dies or becomes untargetable while preserving detailed failures
- Cancel one operation, one Being's operations, or the entire CARAU batch
- Clear or manually retry eligible failures individually, by Being, or across the tracked session
- Automatically removes successful records when their registered operations finish

[h3]User Controls[/h3]
- Tabbed, freely resizable main interface
- Responsive Slots cards enable or disable individual slot types
- Optional display of disabled slots on the Main tab
- Independent Higher-Tier and Same-Tier Quality controls
- Quality threshold slider, numeric input, and quick -10%, -1%, +1%, and +10% adjustments
- Save-specific upgrade, Quality, slot, visibility, retry, and preventative-implant settings with version-safe migration
- New saves use safe defaults without inheriting another game's state
- Optional persistent keyboard shortcut remains global across saves
- Native Surgery & Assembly Priority mirrors Stardeus's save-specific Body Part Procedure Priority (1-5) for new CARAU and manual procedures without rewriting active tasks
- AUMF 1.4.0 owns widget placement, theme-aware panels, tabs, controls, cards, sliders, scrollbars, shortcuts, and lifecycle cleanup

[h3]Diagnostics[/h3]
- Built-in categorized Debug log without routine Player.log noise
- Responsive category controls plus Copy Log and Clear Log
- Copied logs include CARAU version, Stardeus version, and enabled categories
- Every entry preserves its Stardeus game day and time
- Detailed selection, decision, inventory, queue, UI, intent, cleanup, warning, error, tracking, retry, and native-outcome diagnostics

[h2]Credits and Contributions[/h2]
- JangoFett - shared the large save and testing context used to validate CARAU's large-selection and Batch Queue optimizations

[h2]Notes[/h2]
CARAU 1.0 is feature-complete for its current scope. Maintenance releases will remain aligned with supported Stardeus versions.

CARAU only assumes responsibility for operations it schedules. Manually created procedures remain the player's responsibility.

Optional production integration for manufacturing missing parts is reserved for a post-v1.0 expansion through the separately installed Auto Factory mod.
